logo.description: Monochrome (near-black) geometric glyph rendered inline as SVG in the site header, labelled 'Relivo'. Interlocking angular shapes suggesting connected/converging routes. No standalone wordmark asset confirmed beyond the header lockup and favicon.

business_description: Relivo is an open-source, multi-namespace Model Context Protocol (MCP) server written in Go. It mounts five independent MCP servers on a single HTTP mux over the official MCP Go SDK's Streamable HTTP transport, so an MCP client points at one route and that namespace's tools appear. The five namespaces are: memory (durable per-user long-term memory via hybrid RAG, semantic + keyword, over Postgres + pgvector), skills (find and download Agent Skills live from GitHub, nothing cached), gsc (Google Search Console: properties, search-analytics reports, URL inspection, sitemaps), producthunt (Product Hunt v2 GraphQL API: posts, topics, collections, users, plus a raw GraphQL escape hatch), and event (publish/consume Kafka messages and manage topics on Confluent Cloud). Namespaces self-register at startup via init(), so adding one is a single Go package and cmd/server/main.go never changes. Every namespace requires an X-API-Key before dispatch; memory and event additionally scope each caller to their own rows. Advertised scope: 5 namespaces, 42 tools, 1 endpoint, Go 1.26+.
business_model: Open-source developer tool, MIT licensed. Self-hostable (clone, `make run`) with a hosted/managed endpoint available at go-mcp-server-latest.onrender.com behind per-user API keys. No published pricing or paid tier observed on the site; monetization is not stated. A companion web app (relivo-fe.vercel.app) is in beta/development. Treat commercial model as an open question.

brand_aesthetic: Minimal, high-contrast developer-tool aesthetic. Black-on-white, Inter throughout, generous whitespace, large tight headlines (h1 ~60px), and code blocks (mcp.json snippets, register.go) used as primary proof rather than illustration. Feels like modern open-source infra docs (Vercel/Linear/shadcn lineage, Tailwind + shadcn/ui). Quiet and technical: namespace cards with tool counts, a stat line, and copy-pasteable config over marketing imagery. No decorative color, gradients, or stock art.

brand_voice.description: Precise, technical, and understated, written for engineers. Leads with what the system does and the architectural decision behind it, not benefits or hype. Short declarative sentences, exact nouns (namespace, mux, transport, init(), pgvector), and confident opinions stated as constraints ('Opinionated where it counts, out of your way everywhere else'; 'A domain never reaches across another except through internal/mcpx'). Assumes the reader knows MCP, Go, and HTTP. Shows rather than tells: config and code snippets carry the argument.
voice_patterns: Capability-first, one-line namespace descriptions ('6 tools · Memory · Per-user long-term memory')
Architecture stated as a rule or invariant ('Keyed by default', 'Self-registering', 'cmd/server/main.go never changes')
Exact technical nouns over adjectives (Streamable HTTP, hybrid RAG, Postgres + pgvector, slog, net/http mux)
Terse confident asides ('That's it.', 'Point a client at it and go', 'Nothing is cached')
Code and config as the hero (mcp.json, register.go) instead of screenshots or metaphors
Quantified scope claims ('5 namespaces · 42 tools · 1 endpoint · Go 1.26+')

brand_values: Open source and self-hostable: MIT licensed, clone-and-run, no lock-in.
Modularity by design: independent namespaces that self-register; add capability without touching the core.
Isolation and least surprise: a domain never reaches across another except through internal/mcpx.
Secure by default: every namespace requires an X-API-Key before dispatch; per-caller row-level scoping in memory and event.
Standards-first: built on the official MCP Go SDK and Streamable HTTP transport over stdlib net/http.
Developer ergonomics: one endpoint, copy-pasteable config, connect a client in under a minute.
Honesty about state: missing credentials degrade gracefully and tools report the problem rather than failing silently; the companion app is labelled beta.

primary: Developers building AI agents and MCP clients who want ready-made tool servers (memory, skills, live data) behind one endpoint instead of wiring each integration themselves.
Go developers and infra engineers who want a clean, extensible multi-namespace MCP server they can self-host and add namespaces to.
secondary_verticals: SEO/growth tooling teams (via the GSC and Product Hunt namespaces)
Data/event-driven backends (via the Kafka event namespace)

competitors.name: Official MCP reference servers (modelcontextprotocol/servers)
competitors.what_it_does: Anthropic's open-source collection of reference MCP server implementations (filesystem, git, fetch, memory, and more), each typically a standalone server in TypeScript or Python.
competitors.how_it_competes: Overlaps on the 'ready-made MCP tools' need. Relivo differs by unifying multiple domains behind one Go endpoint with a self-registering mux and per-key scoping, rather than one process per server. [comparison inferred from public positioning, needs owner confirmation]

competitors.name: Composio
competitors.what_it_does: Managed platform brokering many connected data sources and tools (incl. Google Search Console, GA4) to agents via a hosted API/MCP layer with auth handling.
competitors.how_it_competes: Overlaps on 'live data sources for agents' (GSC, third-party APIs). Composio is a hosted, closed managed broker; Relivo is a self-hostable MIT-licensed Go server you run and extend yourself. [comparison inferred, needs owner confirmation]

competitor_alternative_categories: Hand-rolling individual MCP servers per integration
Language-specific MCP SDKs used to build bespoke servers from scratch
Standalone single-purpose tool APIs wired directly into an agent
primary_business_goal: Grow adoption of the open-source project (GitHub stars, self-host installs, and connections to the hosted endpoint) as the default multi-namespace MCP server for developers building agents. Commercial/monetization goal is not stated on the site and is an open question.
